comparator.name: Business and Consumer Studies (Bedrijfs- en Consumentenwetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Current WUR programme page and published cohort-2025 curriculum, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The official three-year programme totals 180 EC. Year 1 is a 60-EC common foundation in business, marketing, sociology, law, mathematics, statistics, research and food quality. From year 2 students choose Business or Consumer. The normalized target names neither specialisation, so Business is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break because it appears first in the official programme and legend. The Business route contains 60 EC in year 2, including two genuine restricted choices and the programme-wide professionalisation trajectory, followed in year 3 by 24 EC of named Business study, a 12-EC thesis and 24 EC genuine free choice. Zero-credit General Safety is acknowledged but omitted from the credit-bearing component list.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first programme is the closest feasible response to the neutrally selected Business specialisation. Consumer insight and sustainable/circular transformation are independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions. Pairwise overlaps are 19, 13 and 10 courses respectively, so all alternatives clear the 30-EC distinctness floor. A further business-intelligence route remains evidenced but is not attempted after reaching the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop reflection, presentation, collaboration and professional growth.
Both establish broad foundations in firms, entrepreneurship and markets.
Both use consumer needs and iterative research to develop and assess products.
Both establish research design, statistics and evidence evaluation.
Both develop strategy and organisational change; UCR adds digital transformation.
Both require applied market or product research connecting evidence to innovation.
Both develop accounting and corporate-finance foundations.
Both study microeconomics together with behavioural decision-making.
Both integrate marketing, consumer engagement and responsible strategy.

notes.text: WUR integrates business and consumer science around food and value chains, offers named Business and Consumer specialisations, and requires a 12-EC thesis. UCR can build strong business, consumer, data and sustainability pathways, but does not reproduce WUR’s exact food-quality, sensory-science, decision-science or supply-chain sequence. The alternatives are academically defensible related programmes rather than structural equivalence.
